heading: Validity of the executive function theory of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a meta-analytic review
text: The study found average differences across several executive functions, but these were moderate in size and not universal.
notProven: Executive-function difficulties are neither necessary nor sufficient to explain every case of ADHD.
linea: Meta-analysis with 83 studies, 3,734 ADHD participants and 2,969 controls. Executive-function difficulties are neither necessary nor sufficient to explain every case of ADHD.

heading: Neurocognitive and psychosocial functioning profiles in bipolar disorder and comorbid attention deficit hyperactivity disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis
text: The study compares functioning profiles in bipolar disorder, ADHD, co-occurrence and control groups.
notProven: It does not show that cognitive similarity means diagnostic equivalence and does not by itself resolve differential diagnosis.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis with 34 studies, 31 in meta-analysis. It does not show that cognitive similarity means diagnostic equivalence and does not by itself resolve differential diagnosis.

heading: Current state of evidence on treatments for obsessive-compulsive disorder in children and adolescents: an umbrella review
text: The study places CBT/ERP as the intervention with the strongest evidence and finds moderate evidence for SSRIs; combination treatment may be useful in severe presentations.
notProven: The quality of reviews and studies varies; it does not prescribe an individual treatment.
linea: Umbrella review with 28 systematic reviews/meta-analyses and 24,762 participants. The quality of reviews and studies varies; it does not prescribe an individual treatment.

heading: Cognitive behavioural therapy with exposure and response prevention in the treatment of obsessive-compulsive disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
text: The study found a large pooled effect for CBT+ERP.
notProven: The effect depends strongly on the comparator and allegiance bias; only 8 studies had a low risk of bias.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis with 36 studies and 2,020 patients. The effect depends strongly on the comparator and allegiance bias; only 8 studies had a low risk of bias.

heading: Exposure and response prevention in obsessive-compulsive disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis
text: The study supports the efficacy of ERP compared with control conditions in OCD.
notProven: Protocols and comparators are heterogeneous; the average effect size does not predict an individual's response.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis with 39 RCTs from 30 studies and 1,793 participants. Protocols and comparators are heterogeneous; the average effect size does not predict an individual's response.

heading: Treatment of Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder in Children and Youth: A Meta-Analysis
text: ERP showed benefit compared with waitlist; remote ERP also showed a signal of efficacy; SSRIs were effective and combined treatment may outperform SSRIs alone.
notProven: Effect sizes depend on the comparator and not every trial contributes the same quality of evidence.
linea: Meta-analysis with 71 RCTs. Effect sizes depend on the comparator and not every trial contributes the same quality of evidence.

heading: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Mental Disorders in Adults: A Unified Series of Meta-Analyses
text: The study allows CBT effects to be compared consistently across different mental disorders.
notProven: Effects vary greatly by diagnosis and control-group type; there is no single effect size for 'CBT'.
linea: Unified series of meta-analyses with 375 trials, 423 comparisons and 32,968 participants. Effects vary greatly by diagnosis and control-group type; there is no single effect size for 'CBT'.

heading: Long-term outcomes of cognitive behavioral therapy for anxiety-related disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis
text: The study examines whether CBT effects are maintained beyond the end of treatment.
notProven: Many studies were low quality and evidence at 12 months or longer was limited depending on the disorder.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis with 69 RCTs and 4,118 participants. Many studies were low quality and evidence at 12 months or longer was limited depending on the disorder.

heading: Trauma-focused cognitive behavioural therapy for children and adolescents: a systematic review and meta-analysis
text: The study supports TF-CBT for post-traumatic symptoms in children and adolescents.
notProven: There are risks of bias and publication bias, and the evidence does not justify applying the same protocol without adaptation to every child.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis with 28 RCTs + 33 uncontrolled studies and 4,523 participants. There are risks of bias and publication bias, and the evidence does not justify applying the same protocol without adaptation to every child.

heading: Dyslexia treatment studies: A systematic review and suggestions on testing treatment efficacy with small effects and small samples
text: The study found a modest average effect (about 0.38) and problems involving multiple comparisons, small samples and possible overestimation.
notProven: It does not broadly endorse 'multisensory' programmes, 'brain training' or commercial treatments.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis. It does not broadly endorse 'multisensory' programmes, 'brain training' or commercial treatments.

heading: Domain-general and domain-specific cognitive correlates of developmental dyscalculia: a systematic review of the last two decades' literature
text: The study highlights the importance of both number-specific processes and visuospatial working memory and other domain-general functions.
notProven: It does not demonstrate one single cognitive cause of dyscalculia.
linea: Systematic review of 75 studies. It does not demonstrate one single cognitive cause of dyscalculia.

heading: Domain-General Cognitive Skills in Children with Mathematical Difficulties and Dyscalculia: A Systematic Review of the Literature
text: The study finds group differences in executive functions, attention and processing speed.
notProven: These are group-level correlates and cannot be used as an isolated diagnostic criterion.
linea: Systematic review of 46 studies. These are group-level correlates and cannot be used as an isolated diagnostic criterion.

heading: The Diagnosis and Treatment of Dyscalculia
design: Systematic review, meta-analysis and evidence-based guideline
sample: Multi-database search and meta-analysis of interventions
text: The study supports contextual assessment and treatments directed at specific mathematical difficulties, with a mean effect around 0.52.
notProven: It does not recommend diagnosing from one isolated test or replacing specific mathematics teaching with non-specific training.
linea: Systematic review, meta-analysis and evidence-based guideline. It does not recommend diagnosing from one isolated test or replacing specific mathematics teaching with non-specific training.

heading: Considerations for Intensifying Word-Problem Interventions for Students With Mathematics Difficulty: A Qualitative Umbrella Review of Relevant Meta-Analyses
text: The study identifies variables such as intervention model, number of sessions, group size and risk profile that may moderate outcomes.
notProven: It does not provide one universal recipe and its conclusions depend on earlier meta-analyses.
linea: Qualitative umbrella review of 11 medium-to-high-quality meta-analyses. It does not provide one universal recipe and its conclusions depend on earlier meta-analyses.

heading: The prevalence of specific learning disorder in mathematics and comorbidity with other developmental disorders in primary school-age children
text: Using DSM-5 criteria, the study identified a persistent profile of severe mathematics difficulty in a minority of pupils and frequent co-occurrence with language/communication difficulties.
notProven: One regional study does not establish worldwide prevalence and does not replace individual assessment.
linea: Longitudinal population study with 2,421 schoolchildren. One regional study does not establish worldwide prevalence and does not replace individual assessment.

heading: Existing interventions for the management of different types of dysgraphia or specific learning disorder in written expression: a scoping review
sample: Educational, therapeutic, technological and behavioural interventions
text: The study maps which interventions have been studied for written-expression difficulties/dysgraphia.
notProven: A scoping review describes the available evidence but does not show that every intervention is effective.
linea: Scoping review. A scoping review describes the available evidence but does not show that every intervention is effective.

heading: A systematic review of interventions to improve handwriting
text: The study found more support for handwriting practice than for sensory interventions without specific handwriting practice.
notProven: The evidence is old and heterogeneous and does not correspond exactly to every dysgraphia profile.
linea: Systematic review with 11 controlled studies. The evidence is old and heterogeneous and does not correspond exactly to every dysgraphia profile.

heading: Vocabulary interventions for children with developmental language disorder: a systematic review
text: Explicit interventions targeting phonological and semantic features show the most consistent signal of vocabulary improvement.
notProven: Most studies were medium quality and used individual intervention; generalisation to whole-class settings is limited.
linea: Systematic review of 16 studies. Most studies were medium quality and used individual intervention; generalisation to whole-class settings is limited.

heading: Intervention studies with group design targeting expressive phonology for children with developmental speech and language disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis
text: The study synthesises effects of interventions targeting expressive phonology in speech/language disorders.
notProven: Interventions and diagnostic criteria are heterogeneous; not every phonological difficulty is DLD.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis. Interventions and diagnostic criteria are heterogeneous; not every phonological difficulty is DLD.

heading: Sentence Repetition as a Diagnostic Tool for Developmental Language Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
text: The study evaluates the discriminative ability of sentence-repetition tasks.
notProven: Although they can be useful within a broader assessment battery, they should not become a single diagnostic test.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis. Although sentence-repetition tasks can be useful within a broader assessment battery, they should not become a single diagnostic test.
